albums.blurb: Floating Points is Sam Shepherd, a London electronic producer (with a neuroscience doctorate) who records for Ninja Tune. Crush is his second studio album, following 2015's Elaenia, and it is entirely instrumental: after a 2017 tour supporting the xx, where he played half-hour improvised sets on a Buchla synthesizer and a Korg drum machine, he recorded the album in five weeks using the same rig, trading his debut's live band for pure synthesizers and drum machines. The result swings between modular-synth workouts, string-laden ambient pieces, and dancefloor cuts like "LesAlpx."
albums.reception: Crush holds a Metacritic score of 81, earned Pitchfork's Best New Music designation, and appeared on year-end lists from Pitchfork, DJ Mag, Mixmag, and The Independent.

albums.blurb: Scenery is the New York singer-songwriter's third studio album and her first for ATO Records, arriving four years after The Switch. It distills her blend of classic R&B, pop, and neo-soul into twelve tightly written songs with what Pitchfork described as "1980s soundtrack flourishes" — synth-brushed, guitar-forward soul in the lineage of Prince and post-disco R&B. "Remind Me" and "Look At Me Now" anchor the record.
albums.reception: The album scored 76 on Metacritic, and "Look At Me Now" was nominated for Best R&B Song and Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical at the 2020 Grammy Awards.

albums.blurb: Rodrigo Amarante is a Rio-born songwriter with an unusually wide résumé: co-founder of the Brazilian rock band Los Hermanos, member of the samba collective Orquestra Imperial, one-third of Little Joy with The Strokes' Fabrizio Moretti, and the writer of "Tuyo," the theme to Netflix's Narcos. Drama, released on Polyvinyl in 2021, is his second solo album, following 2014's Cavalo; it moves between Portuguese and English and folds bossa nova, chamber pop, and tropicália-tinged orchestration into a warm, melancholy whole.
albums.reception: Drama placed at No. 45 on NPR Music's 50 Best Albums of 2021 and drew 9/10 scores from both AllMusic and Uncut, with AllMusic calling Amarante "a Tropicália artist for the 21st century."
